items.remediation_detail: PENTEST FINDING: Incomplete X-authentik-* header stripping in nginx forward auth config. authentik-proxy-auth.conf only captures 3 of 10+ headers (username, groups, email). Missing: X-authentik-uid, X-authentik-name, X-authentik-entitlements, X-authentik-jwt, X-authentik-meta-*. Authenticated attacker can inject forged values for uncaptured headers — potential privilege escalation if any backend trusts these. items.remediation_detail: PENTEST FINDING: Overly permissive error_page bypass in nginx forward auth. error_page 403 404 500 502 503 all map to @authentik_bypass which returns 200 (allow). If Authentik outpost is down/unreachable/returns error, ALL 13 proxy-auth-protected services become accessible without authentication. Particularly dangerous: 403 (forbidden) should NOT bypass — it means user lacks authorization. Fix: change error_page 403 to return 403; change 500/502/503 to return 503 instead of 200. Trades availability for security.
items.resolved_by: Rewrote both authentik-proxy-auth.conf and authentik-proxy-locations.conf. Only 404 goes to @authentik_bypass. 403 now blocks (denied by Authentik). 500/502/503/504 → @authentik_fail_closed (returns 503 HTML). Fail-closed for all 13 proxy-auth services.

items.remediation_detail: PENTEST FINDING: RustFS gRPC/internode RPC signature verification uses non-constant-time string comparison (http_auth.rs:114 `!=`) instead of subtle::ConstantTimeEq which is already used for S3 auth in the same codebase. Timing side-channel (CWE-208) could allow signature recovery by an attacker on Docker shared_net. Secondary issues: (a) Future timestamps bypass 5-min replay window via saturating_sub, (b) Error logs leak partial expected signature. Fix: replace `!=` with `constant_time_eq()` from rustfs/src/auth.rs, add abs() timestamp delta check, sanitize error logs.

SAML Assertion Injection via Signature Bypass (CVSS 8.8). When SAML Source has Verify Assertion Signature enabled but Verify Response Signature disabled, attacker can prepend unsigned malicious assertion to legitimate signed one. Authentik then trusts and processes the forged assertion instead of the legitimate one. Our version 2025.12.4 includes the fix — no action required.

(2) CVE-2026-42530 — use-after-free in HTTP/3 (severity 'major'); fixed 1.31.2+. (3) CVE-2026-42055 — buffer overflow in ngx_http_proxy_v2_module + ngx_http_grpc_module, remote unauthenticated worker-process restart; fixed 1.31.2+ / 1.30.3+. Left pending: operator host-package upgrade. | 2026-07-11 RE-SCAN (cycle-16 batch-25): three ADDITIONAL 2026 nginx CVEs surfaced, ALL cleared by the SAME >=1.31.2 fix target (no change to the remediation) -- folded in for lineage: CVE-2026-48142 (LOW, buffer OVERREAD in ngx_http_charset_module, info-disclosure, affects 0.3.50-1.31.1, fix 1.31.2+/1.30.3+ -- charset module is compiled by default so in active surface), CVE-2026-42926 (MEDIUM, HTTP/2 request injection in ngx_http_proxy_module, affects 1.29.4-1.30.0, fix 1.31.0+/1.30.1+), CVE-2026-42946 (MEDIUM, buffer overread in ngx_http_scgi_module + ngx_http_uwsgi_module, affects 0.8.42-1.30.0, fix 1.31.0+/1.30.1+ -- SCGI/uWSGI not used by nOS vhosts, latent). nginx >=1.31.2 clears the entire 2026 set (42945/42530/42055/9256 + 48142/42926/42946). items.remediation_detail: Gitea 1.25.5 (2026-03-13) is the LAST 1.25.x release — there is no 1.25.6; the 1.25 line is END-OF-LIFE and every security fix from 2026-04 onward landed only in 1.26.x with NO backport. UNAUTH HEADLINE: CVE-2026-27771 (CRITICAL, fix 1.26.2) — Gitea's built-in container/OCI + Composer package registry serves PRIVATE packages/images to ANONYMOUS (unauthenticated) pull requests; ~4-yr-old flaw, ~31k internet-facing instances. In nOS the package registry is ENABLED (Gitea default; no [packages] ENABLED=false in the role) AND the Gitea Traefik route is native_oidc (traefik_auth_modes.gitea=oidc) -> NOT forward-auth gated (200 OK at the edge, Gitea owns its own login), so the registry endpoints are reachable by anonymous clients via the LAN/Tailscale Traefik route = a genuine unauthenticated-endpoint exposure (latent if no private packages stored yet, but the line is EOL). ALSO AFFECTED (all fixed only in 1.26.x): CVE-2026-22874 (CRITICAL 9.6 webhook SSRF, incomplete private-IP allow-list, fix 1.26.3; authenticated), CVE-2026-28699/28744 (HIGH OAuth2/Bearer token scope-enforcement bypass, fix 1.26.2), CVE-2026-28737 (HIGH stored XSS in glTF 3D viewer, fix 1.26.0), CVE-2026-22555 (HIGH org-fork CanCreateOrgRepo bypass, fix 1.26.0), CVE-2026-26231 (HIGH allow-maintainer-edits authz bypass, fix 1.26.2), CVE-2026-24791 (HIGH public-only token bypass, fix 1.26.2), CVE-2026-20779 (HIGH 2FA TOTP replay race, fix 1.26.3). NOT APPLICABLE in nOS: CVE-2026-20896 (CRITICAL 9.8 X-WEBAUTH-USER impersonation via the image default REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES=*) needs Gitea reverse-proxy header auth (ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION) to be ON — nOS does NOT enable it (Gitea uses native_oidc, no header-trust block), so the precondition fails; set REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES to loopback anyway as defense-in-depth. REMEDIATION: bump gitea_version 1.25.5 -> 1.26.4 (latest stable; 1.26.2 still misses the three 1.26.3 criticals; skip 1.26.3 itself — repo-code-page 'context deadline' regression). Interim: require auth for all package/registry reads. Already-tracked CVE-2026-gitea-template-traversal (REM-028) + CVE-2026-20897/20750/20888 (REM-066) remain fixed at 1.25.5. | 2026-07-02 RE-SCAN (cycle-16 re-check): STILL PENDING, disposition unchanged. Pin unchanged at 1.25.5 (default.config.yml + role default in sync); traefik_auth_modes.gitea=oidc (200 at edge, registry endpoints anonymously reachable = the unauth CVE-2026-27771 exposure persists), 127.0.0.1:3003 loopback.

items.remediation_detail: Portainer 2.27 LTS reached END-OF-LIFE in Nov 2025 (superseded by 2.33 LTS) — pin 2.27.3 receives ZERO further security patches. A 2026 container-escape cluster was disclosed: CVE-2026-44848 + CVE-2026-44849 (both CRITICAL 9.4) — an AUTHENTICATED non-admin user with Docker/Swarm endpoint access reaches host-root RCE (missing authz on Docker plugin endpoints; Swarm service create/update skips 6-7 of 7 security checks -> Linux caps / bind-mount). CVE-2026-44850/44881/44883/44882 (HIGH) add bind-mount-restriction bypass / Git-symlink arbitrary file read / JWT-in-URL token leak / k8s middleware authz bypass. NUANCE: the formal OSV/GHSA affected ranges all START at 2.33.0, so a version-keyed scanner reports 2.27.3 'clean' — but the advisory prose states the vulnerable validation logic 'has never' existed (every Swarm-capable release), so 2.27.3's paths are very likely exploitable, just officially un-fixed on the EOL line (hence confidence: medium on the cluster, high on the EOL fact). SEPARATELY the 2.27.x container IMAGE base layer almost certainly carries CVE-2025-15467 (HIGH 8.8, pre-auth OpenSSL CMS/PKCS#7 stack overflow -> DoS/RCE) with no rebuilt 2.27.x image. nOS MITIGATION (reduces, not removes): the host-RCE bugs need an authenticated Portainer session; Portainer is Tier-1 admin-only, native_oidc behind Authentik, 127.0.0.1:9002 loopback, and reaches Docker via docker-socket-proxy (REM-001) not the raw socket. REMEDIATION: bump portainer_version 2.27.3 -> a supported LTS (2.33.8; or STS 2.39.2 / 2.41.0), carrying the full 44848..44885 fix cluster AND the rebuilt-OpenSSL base image. Note: already-tracked CVE-2025-49593 (REM-034) is only partially closed on 2.27.3 — its Moderate header-leak variant (GHSA-h5jw-8c32-xfv6) fixes in 2.27.7.

items.remediation_detail: Four new May-Jun 2026 MariaDB CVEs place 11.8.6 inside the version-affected range: CVE-2026-49261 (CVSS 10.0, RCE via shell commands embedded in a joiner node name when wsrep_notify_cmd is set; fix 11.8.8), CVE-2026-48165 (8.0, SUPER user injects shell via wsrep_sst_donor / wsrep_sst_receive_address; fix 11.8.8), CVE-2026-48163 (8.0, wsrep_sst_rsync parameter injection; fix 11.8.8), CVE-2026-44168 (8.0, mariabackup-SST param injection on donor; fix 11.8.7). nOS DISPOSITION — MITIGATED: ALL FOUR are exclusively Galera Cluster (wsrep) vulnerabilities living in wsrep_notify_cmd / wsrep_sst_rsync / wsrep_sst_donor / mariabackup-SST. The official mariadb image runs STANDALONE by default (no wsrep_on=ON, no wsrep_provider) and nOS runs a single loopback (127.0.0.1:3306) + internal-net, password-authenticated instance with NO Galera cluster. MariaDB's own guidance + the upstream GHSAs + Singapore CSA AL-2026-078 scope the advisory to Galera users and confirm standalone deployments are NOT exploitable; the CVSS-10.0 pre-auth network vector only materializes inside an active Galera cluster. So there is NO reachable unpatched HIGH/CRITICAL in this deployment. RECOMMENDATION (hygiene, low urgency): bump mariadb_version 11.8.6 -> 11.8.8 — a non-breaking patch-level move within 11.8 stable that clears all four from image-tag scanners (which flag 11.8.6 regardless of wsrep config). No NEW HIGH/CRITICAL beyond this Galera cluster. A separate 11.8.7 batch now version-flags 11.8.6 but is N/A to nOS: CVE-2026-44170 (NVD 9.8 CONNECT-engine REST Xcurl arg-injection = Windows-only + CONNECT/REST not enabled), CVE-2026-44173 (SELECT..INTO OUTFILE FILE-priv check skip on subquery-only FROM, authed, marginal), CVE-2026-44171 (mbstream/mariabackup path-traversal), CVE-2026-44172 (big5 client-lib escaping), CVE-2026-3494 (audit-plugin bypass) — all fixed 11.8.7, none reach the loopback/standalone/Linux/no-CONNECT surface. Bump target stays 11.8.6->11.8.8 (clears BOTH the Galera set and the 11.8.7 batch in one move). items.remediation_detail: CVE-2026-50141 / GHSA-g7mm-9vx7-jm7h (HIGH; CWE-290 authentication-bypass-by-spoofing + CWE-639): an AUTHENTICATED Woodpecker agent can inject a forged agent_id into gRPC metadata; the server validates the agent JWT but then discards the verified identity and trusts the client-supplied agent_id -> cross-tenant agent impersonation. Affected 3.0.0-3.14.0, fixed 3.14.1 (interim workaround WOODPECKER_DISABLE_USER_AGENT_REGISTRATION=true). MITIGATED in nOS on three axes: (1) the gRPC endpoint binds 127.0.0.1:9060 loopback (compose: 127.0.0.1:{{woodpecker_grpc_port}}:9000) -> not LAN-exposed; (2) exploitation requires a VALID authenticated agent JWT, so the pre-auth surface is nil, and nOS typically runs a single agent on the same host so 'cross-tenant impersonation' has no second tenant to cross; (3) the running image floats PAST the fix -- the woodpecker_version role default is already v3.14.1 and default.config.yml pins the floating major tag 'v3' which resolves to the latest 3.x (>=3.14.1). VERSION-PIN SHADOW CAVEAT (cf. memory version-pins-default-config-shadow.md): config-wins means the EFFECTIVE pin is the floating 'v3', NOT the explicit role default v3.14.1 -- the fix is present only because 'v3' currently floats to >=3.14.1, and the exact running build is non-deterministic. RECOMMENDATION: set default.config.yml woodpecker_version to an explicit >=3.14.1 (e.g. 'v3.14.1', matching the role default) to make the fix deterministic and close the floating-tag supply-chain reproducibility gap. Distinct from REM-002 (woodpecker docker-socket pipeline-escape, still pending). Tier 2; web UI route is oidc (Gitea OAuth app-auth, NOT forward-auth gated; 127.0.0.1:8060 loopback). [RESOLVED 2026-07-13: pin bumped in default.config.yml, live-verified — running image + smoke 49/49.]

May-2026 dnsmasq CERT/CC cluster (VU#471747): six CVEs fixed in 2.92rel2 (and the upcoming 2.93). Our host pin 2.91 is AFFECTED. APPLICABLE to nOS's config (DNS forwarder, no DNSSEC, no DHCP): CVE-2026-2291 (CVSS 7.3 HIGH, AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N — heap buffer overflow in extract_name() while parsing DNS RESPONSES -> false DNS-cache injection / redirect to attacker IP, or DoS; UNAUTHENTICATED + network) and CVE-2026-5172 (heap OOB read in extract_addresses() on a malformed DNS response -> crash/DoS). Reachable because tasks/dnsmasq.yml binds the LAN interface by DEFAULT — dnsmasq_lan_access defaults true, so listen-address=127.0.0.1,<en0 LAN IP> + bind-interfaces — and dnsmasq forwards every non-{dev.local} query upstream, so a LAN/Tailscale client that makes it resolve an attacker-controlled domain feeds malformed responses into the vulnerable parsers. NOT applicable to nOS: CVE-2026-4890/4891 (DNSSEC-validation infinite-loop DoS + heap OOB read — nOS sets NO `dnssec` directive in dnsmasq.conf, validation disabled), CVE-2026-4892 (DHCPv6 heap OOB write -> local root RCE — nOS runs DNS-only, no `dhcp-range`/DHCP server), CVE-2026-4893 (RFC-7871 client-subnet source-check bypass — `add-subnet` not configured). dnsmasq is a HOST Homebrew package (community.general.homebrew state:present in tasks/dnsmasq.yml; the dnsmasq_version='2.91' var is documentation only, not enforced — like REM-035 nginx / REM-024 ollama there is no pinnable image). REMEDIATION: (1) operator-side `brew upgrade dnsmasq` to >=2.92rel2 once the formula ships it (Homebrew may still carry 2.91); (2) defence-in-depth — set dnsmasq_lan_access=false to bind 127.0.0.1 only and remove all LAN reach if LAN-wide *.dev.local resolution is not required.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-16 batch-6 unauthenticated_endpoint_scan finding (NOT a CVE — no Grafana Alloy security advisory exists in the 12-mo window; OSV/GHSA/NVD return no alloy-specific CVE). Grafana Alloy is HOST-installed via Homebrew (grafana-alloy formula, run under `brew services` — files/anatomy/plugins/alloy-base) and its config is rendered to {{homebrew_prefix}}/etc/grafana-alloy/config.alloy from files/observability/alloy/config.alloy.j2 by tasks/observability.yml. The `otelcol.receiver.otlp "default"` block binds grpc endpoint = 0.0.0.0:{{alloy_otlp_grpc_port|4317}} AND http endpoint = 0.0.0.0:{{alloy_otlp_http_port|4318}}, with NO auth extension configured (unauthenticated by design — 'public OTLP, apps -> Alloy' per default.config.yml). Because Alloy is a HOST process (not a Docker container with a 127.0.0.1:<port> publish mapping), the 0.0.0.0 bind means the OS listens on EVERY host interface -> the receiver is reachable from the LAN and over Tailscale, not just loopback. EXPLOITABLE (rated exploitable, not theoretical): any LAN/Tailscale peer can POST OTLP traces/metrics/logs into the observability pipeline with no credential -> (a) telemetry INJECTION/SPOOFING that pollutes Grafana dashboards and poisons the trace/audit lineage the A8 conductor agent consumes (false operational signals); (b) unbounded-ingestion RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION DoS against the Alloy->Tempo/Loki/Prometheus chain. Severity capped at MEDIUM: no host compromise, no secret/data READ (the receiver only accepts pushes), and the OTLP sinks (Tempo 127.0.0.1:3200/4327/4328, Loki 127.0.0.1:3100, Prometheus 127.0.0.1:9090) are all loopback-bound so the blast radius is pipeline data-integrity + availability, not those backends directly. The Alloy debug UI (alloy_ui_port 12345) is NOT exposed — it binds loopback by default (the alloy_self scrape targets localhost:12345). MITIGATING/AGGRAVATING CONTEXT: no nOS task configures a host firewall on macOS (the macOS application firewall is off by default and unmanaged here), and on Linux the only firewall is the OPT-IN, default-disabled roles/pazny.linux.hardening ufw -> on a stock install nothing else blocks 4317/4318. REMEDIATION (defense-in-depth, two copies must change together): if only on-host applications emit traces, change both endpoints to 127.0.0.1 in files/observability/alloy/config.alloy.j2 AND files/anatomy/plugins/alloy-base/templates/config.alloy.j2; if cross-host app telemetry IS required, keep 0.0.0.0 but front it with a host firewall rule scoped to the trusted subnet (ufw allow from <net> to any port 4317,4318) and/or add an OTLP auth extension. Cleanest knob: introduce an alloy_otlp_bind_addr var (default 127.0.0.1) so the bind is operator-controlled like services_lan_access.

Cycle-16 batch-6 finding (supply-chain hygiene, NOT a live CVE — Puter has NO published security advisories: github.com/HeyPuter/puter/security/advisories is empty and there is no OSV/NVD hit for HeyPuter/Puter in the 12-mo window, so the CVE leg is CLEAN). files/puter/Dockerfile begins `FROM ghcr.io/heyputer/puter:latest` — a FLOATING upstream base tag. The puter_version="v2.5.1" var (default.config.yml, source-of-truth; role default is 'latest') only labels the LOCALLY-BUILT image nos/puter:v2.5.1 — it does NOT pin the upstream code, which is pulled fresh from :latest at every `docker compose build`. The default.config.yml comment ('Dockerfile FROM pinned separately') is therefore INACCURATE: the FROM is unpinned. Consequence: builds are non-reproducible and there is a supply-chain exposure window — a regressed or compromised upstream :latest push is adopted on the next blank/rebuild with no review or version gate. Same floating-tag reproducibility class already flagged for woodpecker 'v3' (REM-105), superset 6.0.0-dev, and paperclip sha-<commit> (REM-097). PERIMETER (unaffected by this finding, recorded for the probe): puter's Traefik route is forward_auth (traefik_auth_modes.puter=proxy -> authentik@file gates every endpoint) + 127.0.0.1:5050 loopback bind (services_lan_access=false) + Tier 3; the /healthcheck endpoint is intentionally public ({"ok":true}) but only reachable on loopback / behind the Authentik wall. REMEDIATION: pin the Dockerfile base to an immutable upstream reference — `FROM ghcr.io/heyputer/puter:<tag>@sha256:<digest>` matching the intended puter_version — so rebuilds are deterministic and upstream changes are reviewed before adoption; correct the misleading default.config.yml comment at the same time. — CLOSED 2026-07-20 as obsolete: the Puter service was removed from nOS (nOS face replaced it as the web-desktop), so the local nos/puter build and its floating `FROM ghcr.io/heyputer/puter:latest` base tag no longer exist.

Cycle-16 batch-7 CVE scan (n8n). A June-24-2026 n8n advisory cluster (4 HIGH, CVSS 7.1-7.6) is fixed only in 2.27.4 / 2.28.1 on the 2.x line (and 1.x backport 1.123.61); the pinned n8n_version 2.26.2 is < 2.27.4 = AFFECTED on all four (OSV had not yet indexed them at scan time because they are <2 days old, but the GitHub Security Advisory API vulnerable_version_range strings are explicit '< 2.27.4'). The other three need an authenticated member/editor account + a NON-DEFAULT config: GHSA-mq3m-f8x3-579w (7.6, cross-issuer JWT sub-only binding -> user impersonation, only when token-exchange + multiple trusted issuers configured), GHSA-q3j5-8vrg-4p9q (7.1, HTTP-Header-Auth shared-credential secret leaked in $request.headers during pagination-expression eval, only when N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm), GHSA-h44j-f5r5-ph73 (7.1, 'Allowed HTTP Request Domains' bypass via the AI-Agents MCP connector -> exfiltrate a shared-credential secret to an attacker URL, only when N8N_ENABLED_MODULES=agents). Same bump also clears 5 MODERATE advisories (external-secrets exposure/permission-bypass GHSA-2434-3x6q-8r99 / GHSA-jp7m-xcgx-57qm, MySQL-v1-node SQLi GHSA-hwmj-qg4v-cvg9, cross-project folder assignment GHSA-2xgm-wc4g-5jvg, data-table upload disk-exhaustion DoS GHSA-w867-jm58-p9pv). COVERED at 2.26.2 (no action, recorded for lineage): CVE-2026-54305 (CRITICAL, CVSS 9.9, Dynamic-Credentials cross-tenant EE credential takeover) -- 2.26.2 was the release cut specifically to fix it; CVE-2026-54303 (HIGH, reflected XSS, fix 2.24.0). PERIMETER: n8n's Traefik route is native_oidc (traefik_auth_modes.n8n=oidc -> 200 at the edge, n8n serves its own login + API, NO forward-auth wall) so once any authed user plants the polluted workflow the proto-pollution data-exposure/enumeration leg IS reachable by an anonymous caller over the LAN/Tailscale route; 127.0.0.1:5678 loopback host bind. ACTION: bump n8n_version 2.26.2->2.28.1 in default.config.yml (source of truth, line ~1395) AND roles/pazny.n8n/defaults/main.yml (the version-pin shadow -- both must move together per the version-pins-default-config-shadow rule); same-major 2.x migrate-on-start, validate workflows on the next run. 2.27.4 is the minimum safe version; 2.28.1 is the latest 2.x and additionally clears the 5 moderates. Cycle-16 batch-8 unauthenticated_endpoint_scan (bone). Bone's read endpoints GET /api/services, GET /api/health/aggregate and GET /api/status carry NO require_scope() dependency (files/anatomy/bone/main.py lines 172/144/181) — unlike every operational route (run-tag / state / migrations / upgrades / coexistence, all Depends(require_scope(...)) since the Track-B 2026-04-26 JWT cutover that retired the legacy BONE_SECRET channel). Bone is a Tier-1 manifest service with domain_var=bone_domain (api.<tld>) + port_var=bone_port (state/manifest.yml), and traefik_auth_modes.bone='none' (roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml, commented 'JWT-validated API' — so NO authentik@file forward-auth middleware is attached). The Traefik file provider therefore renders an api.<tld> router with NO auth wall in front of these ungated reads. RESULT: an UNAUTHENTICATED LAN/Tailscale caller resolving api.<tld> can GET /api/services (returns the entire service-registry.json verbatim: every service id, internal hostname, port, version, health URL, domain), GET /api/health/aggregate (fan-out health of all ~37 registered services with the same per-service detail), and GET /api/status (instance_name='nOS', the nOS VERSION file contents, host gethostname(), services_count). This is a CWE-200 information-disclosure / recon exposure: the version map tells an attacker exactly which per-service CVEs apply, and the internal hostnames/ports/URLs feed SSRF + lateral-movement targeting. No credentials, no RCE, and it requires reaching the trusted-network perimeter (the api.<tld> route, not the public internet unless DNS+cert are public) -> MEDIUM. The uvicorn --host 127.0.0.1:8099 loopback bind blocks direct host access but does NOT block the routed api.<tld> edge. FIX: add Depends(require_scope('nos:state:read')) to the services() / status() / health_aggregate() handlers (KEEP the O(1) /api/health liveness probe ungated — docker healthcheck, launchd KeepAlive probe, and tools/nos-smoke.py all need an unauthenticated liveness ping), OR flip traefik_auth_modes.bone from 'none' to 'proxy' (forward-auth) — the JWT-on-read approach is preferred because it preserves Bone's bearer-token API model for legitimate machine callers (Pulse, Wing, conductor) that already mint Authentik JWTs. DEP NOTE (folded here, no separate item): bone requirements.txt pins fastapi>=0.115 + uvicorn[standard]>=0.32 + PyJWT[crypto]>=2.9 as unpinned >= floors, so the June-2026 Starlette/python-multipart cluster (CVE-2026-54283 form-data limit-bypass DoS, fix Starlette 0.49.1; CVE-2026-53539 python-multipart quadratic-complexity DoS, fix 0.0.30; CVE-2026-48710 'BadHost' Host-header auth bypass) rides on whatever pip resolves at venv-build time. The three ungated routes are GET-only with NO form/multipart parsing -> the two DoS legs are N/A, and Bone registers no Starlette TrustedHostMiddleware -> BadHost is N/A; but pin the deps to a lockfile (mirroring the wing composer.lock discipline) for supply-chain reproducibility. PyJWT CLUSTER (folded here, re-scan 2026-07-08): bone pins PyJWT[crypto]>=2.9 (unpinned floor). CVE-2026-48526 (Improper Authentication / RS-HS algorithm confusion — forge a token by supplying the RSA public key as the HMAC secret; fix 2.13.0) is CODE-MITIGATED: verify_token() in files/anatomy/bone/auth.py:149-158 calls jwt.decode(..., algorithms=["RS256"]) with a fixed single-algorithm allowlist and an RSA PyJWK from Authentik JWKS, so an HS256 token is rejected before verification — NOT exploitable. CVE-2026-32597 (crit-header extensions accepted, fix 2.13.0) + CVE-2026-48525 (unauthenticated DoS via unbounded Base64URL decode of the payload segment in a b64=false detached JWS BEFORE signature rejection, fix 2.13.0) are LOW-impact residuals (48525 is the only unauth leg — reachable at any require_scope() route since decode runs pre-rejection, but bounded by the 5s/loopback posture). Bump the floor to PyJWT>=2.13.0 and pin ALL bone deps (fastapi/uvicorn/httpx/PyYAML/PyJWT) to a lockfile — same supply-chain-reproducibility ask as the Starlette/python-multipart note above.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-16 batch-9 (2026-06-29) unauthenticated_endpoint_scan. items.remediation_detail: Cycle-16 batch-11 (2026-07-01) CVE scan. RustFS shipped a June-2026 advisory cluster (published 2026-06-27 and 2026-06-29, AFTER the 2026-06-20 REM-093 scan) fixed ONLY in the new 1.0.0-beta release line, so the pinned rustfs_version 1.0.0-alpha.93 AND the REM-093 bump target 1.0.0-alpha.98 are BOTH below the fix and remain affected -> REM-093's alpha.98 target is now STALE and the real fix target advances to 1.0.0-beta.9. CLUSTER: (1) CVE-2026-55188 (HIGH CVSS 8.2, GHSA-796f-j7xp-hwf4) -- the ListRemoteTargetHandler bucket-replication admin API checks only that request credentials EXIST, not that the caller holds replication/admin permission, so any authenticated user with no effective permissions can list a bucket's remote replication targets, and the returned BucketTarget objects INCLUDE the remote target access key + secret key (credential disclosure); affected 1.0.0-alpha.1..<beta.9, fix beta.9. (2) CVE-2026-49991 (HIGH CVSS 8.6, GHSA-f4vq-9ffr-m8m3) -- Snowball auto-extract path traversal: an authenticated user holding only PutObject on their own bucket injects objects ACROSS bucket boundaries (multi-tenant isolation break, CWE-22); affected through 1.0.0-beta.4, fixed in the beta line. (3) CVE-2026-55189 (HIGH CVSS 7.7, GHSA-3g29-xff2-92vp) -- the FTP frontend RETR/SIZE/MDTM/CWD handlers dispatch straight to the storage backend WITHOUT the IAM authorization call the FTP write/list handlers (and the whole HTTP S3 path) use, so any FTP-authenticated user (even one whose IAM policy carries an explicit Deny on s3:GetObject) can read + stat + probe any object in any bucket regardless of policy; affected 1.0.0-alpha.1..<beta.9, fix beta.9 -- reachable ONLY if the RustFS FTP frontend is enabled (nOS does NOT enable it by default -> latent here). (4) CVE-2026-55838 (MEDIUM CVSS 4.3, GHSA-f5cv-v44x-2xgf) -- /rustfs/admin/v3/metrics skips validate_admin_request, so any IAM user (even one scoped to only their own bucket) reads server-wide operational metrics (disk I/O, network throughput, scanner-cycle timing, cluster RPC state); affected <=1.0.0-beta.7, fix beta.7/beta.9. (5) GHSA-7gcx-wg4x-q9x6 (CRITICAL) 'Incomplete fix: Critical Stored XSS in Preview Modal' -- the earlier CVE-2026-27822 console preview-modal stored XSS (nominally covered by alpha.93 at its alpha.83 fix) had an INCOMPLETE fix; the COMPLETE fix lands only in the beta line. This is the PROBE-RELEVANT leg (unauthenticated_endpoint_scan focus): the RustFS web console (9001) is the ONLY Traefik-routed RustFS surface and its router carries traefik_auth_modes['rustfs']='none' (NO authentik@file forward-auth), relying solely on RustFS's own beta-grade credential login -- so a stored XSS firing JavaScript in the console context steals the S3 admin access/secret keys from localStorage -> full console/account takeover, an especially sharp risk with install_rustfs=true (Tier-1 storage ON by default). PROBE verdict: the genuinely-UNAUTHENTICATED leg remains CVE-2026-40937 (REM-093, notification-target webhook config, still valid); the rest of the June cluster is authenticated (FTP/IAM users) EXCEPT the auth:none-console-reachable stored XSS. nOS MITIGATION lowering real-world reach: the S3 + admin API (RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET) binds 127.0.0.1:9010 loopback / Docker shared_net only (NOT external); only the console (9001) is edge-routed; the FTP frontend and bucket replication are NOT configured by default (so 55189 + 55188 are latent). ACTION: bump rustfs_version 1.0.0-alpha.93 -> 1.0.0-beta.9 (default.config.yml source-of-truth + mirror roles/pazny.rustfs/defaults/main.yml per version-pins-default-config-shadow) -- clears the entire June cluster AND supersedes REM-093's alpha.98 target with margin; ALSO gate the console router with authentik@file forward-auth (flip traefik_auth_modes['rustfs']='proxy') as defense-in-depth against the console-XSS class. Already covered by the current alpha.93 pin, recorded for lineage (fix <= alpha.83, no incremental action beyond the incomplete-fix caveat): CVE-2026-27822 (Critical Stored XSS console preview modal, fix alpha.83 -- but the COMPLETE fix needs beta.9, see above) + CVE-2026-27607 (presigned POST-policy validation bypass -> arbitrary object write + content-length/content-type-constraint bypass, fix alpha.83). Supersedes/extends REM-093 (same rustfs_version bump, higher target).

The pinned ntfy_version v2.22.0 (roles/pazny.ntfy/defaults/main.yml) is version-flagged by GHSA-j8hr-p342-xrmh -- a stored XSS via SVG attachment preview: an attacker uploads a crafted SVG, and when a victim previews that attachment in the ntfy web UI the SVG's script executes same-origin (blob-URL preview). items.remediation_detail: Cycle-16 batch-25 RE-SCAN (2026-07-11, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). Vaultwarden 1.36.0 (the current release, superseding the 1.35.x line) ships a cluster of security advisories NOT present in the pinned vaultwarden_version 1.35.8 (default.config.yml + role default in sync); several are UNAUTHENTICATED = the probe-relevant leg the prior batch-11 REM-095 disposition (resolved at 1.35.8) did not yet cover. Advisories (private/pending-CVE at release, GHSA-tracked): (1) SSO Login CSRF -- GHSA-pfp2-jhgq-6hg5 + GHSA-w6h6-8r66-hcv7 (UNAUTH, cross-site request forgery against the SSO auth callback -> can bind/complete an SSO login flow chosen by the attacker); (2) User/Organization Enumeration -- GHSA-hxqh-ff5p-wfr3 (UNAUTH info-disclosure, distinguishes existing vs non-existing accounts/orgs); (3) SSRF via Icon Endpoint -- GHSA-72vh-x5jq-m82g (UNAUTH server-side request forgery via the /icons/ favicon fetcher -> internal-network probing); (4) SSO Existing-User Binding -- GHSA-j4j8-gpvj-7fqr + GHSA-6x5c-84vm-5j56 (auth-bypass class, binds an SSO identity onto an existing local user). nOS runs Vaultwarden with SSO via Authentik OIDC, so the SSO-flow legs (1)+(4) are in the applicable surface. ALREADY COVERED at 1.35.8 (no action, logged for lineage): CVE-2026-43912 (cross-organization data access, fixed 1.35.5) -- 1.35.8 > 1.35.5. items.remediation_detail: Cycle-16 batch-25 RE-SCAN (2026-07-11, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). CVE-2026-5757 (CERT/CC VU#518910, 'Ollama GGUF Quantization Remote Memory Leak') -- an UNAUTHENTICATED remote information-disclosure flaw in Ollama's model quantization engine, DISTINCT from the covered CVE-2026-7482 'Bleeding Llama' (REM-096, /api/create GGUF loader OOB-read, fixed 0.17.1). Here the quantization engine trusts tensor metadata in a user-supplied GGUF file header without verifying it against the actual data size: an attacker uploads a crafted GGUF and triggers quantization, causing an out-of-bounds heap read whose leaked bytes are written into a NEW model layer, which Ollama's registry API can then /api/push to an attacker-controlled server -> full heap exfiltration (env vars/API keys/system prompts/other users' conversation data), same impact class as CVE-2026-7482. STATUS: UNPATCHED -- per CERT/CC the vendor could not be reached to coordinate and no fix release exists (zero-day; interim guidance = restrict/disable the model-upload + quantization functionality in any environment exposed to untrusted users). This is NOT closable by a version bump (unlike REM-096), so it parallels the REM-064 'no upstream fix' pattern -- the control is perimeter, not a patch. nOS MITIGATION (the decisive control): Ollama is the HOST Homebrew install (roles/pazny.openclaw), and its launchd plist (roles/pazny.openclaw/templates/com.ollama.agent.plist.j2) hard-sets OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434 -- the API (incl. the /api/create quantization + /api/push registry endpoints) binds LOOPBACK ONLY, not 0.0.0.0, so the unauthenticated attack surface is not reachable from the LAN/Tailscale; only the on-host OpenClaw gateway consumes it. There is NO ollama_version var to pin (same host-install reality as REM-024/REM-096). NOT applicable: CVE-2026-42248/42249 (Windows auto-updater signature-verify RCE) -- macOS/Linux Homebrew build. RESIDUAL RISK: a local/on-host process (or a compromised OpenClaw agent) could still trigger it; when an upstream fix ships, the floating brew state=latest install will pick it up automatically (verify via REM-024). ACTION: keep OLLAMA_HOST bound to 127.0.0.1 (already enforced -- do NOT set OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0); operator-side brew-currency watch for the eventual fix release (cross-ref REM-024).
items.resolution: No upstream fix — CVE-2026-5757 (GGUF quantization heap leak) is UNPATCHED; CERT/CC (VU#518910) could not reach the vendor. Distinct from CVE-2026-7482 Bleeding Llama (fixed 0.17.1 < our 0.30.7). Vendor-blocked like FreePBX: unfixable in the current upstream. Residual controls (loopback 127.0.0.1 bind + SSO gate) noted but do NOT constitute a fix. Re-evaluate on an ollama patch.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-16 batch-28 (2026-07-15, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). The July-8-2026 Traefik release wave (v3.6.22 + v3.6.23) version-flags the pinned traefik_image_version v3.6.21 (default.config.yml + role default in sync). PRIMARY: CVE-2026-54763 (GHSA-x677-9fxg-v5c5, HIGH -- ForwardAuth-specific base CVSS 9.1, BasicAuth/DigestAuth base 7.5; affects v3 <= v3.6.21 and <= v3.7.5; fixed v3.6.22 / v3.7.6 / v2.11.51) = an INCOMPLETE FIX for CVE-2026-33433 (REM-025, resolved). The original patch strips spoofed auth headers with Go's Header.Del, which canonicalizes via textproto.CanonicalMIMEHeaderKey -- that treats '-' as a word separator but NOT '_', so an attacker can inject UNDERSCORE-VARIANT header names (X_authentik_username, X_authentik_groups) that survive Traefik's strip and reach the backend intact; exploitable when the backend normalizes '_'=='-' (PHP/CGI/WSGI $_SERVER -> HTTP_X_AUTHENTIK_*, nginx underscores_in_headers on, Tomcat/servlet, ASGI). nOS is IN the applicable surface: middlewares.yml.j2 defines the 'authentik' forwardAuth middleware with trustForwardHeader:true + authResponseHeaders X-authentik-username/uid/email/name/groups -- the X-authentik-groups header drives the RBAC tier mapping, so an underscore-spoof is an identity/authorization forgery on the core SSO gate. COMPANION: CVE-2026-54764 (MEDIUM, CVSS v3 5.8 -- ForwardAuth X-Forwarded-Proto injection: an unauth client sends 'X-Forwarded-Proto: https' over plain HTTP so Traefik forwards X-Forwarded-Port:443 to the auth service, bypassing port-based authorization checks; same trustForwardHeader:true surface; fixed v3.6.22). N/A (recorded for lineage): GHSA-cxjq-mrr5-89rv (HIGH 7.8, ReplacePathRegex auth-bypass via post-replacement path traversal, no CVE assigned, fixed v3.6.23) -- grep-confirmed nOS uses NO ReplacePathRegex/replacePath middleware anywhere (roles/pazny.traefik middlewares are authentik forwardAuth + security-headers + https-redirect + compress + wing-edge + optional miniflux redirectRegex); GHSA-42cj-m3vj-89wv (CRD IngressRouteTCP ServersTransport cross-provider bypass) + GHSA-qq9q-x9w4-chhj / GHSA-6p8f-p8j2-rqmv (Gateway API HTTPRoute namespace confusion) -- Kubernetes-CRD/Gateway-provider ONLY, N/A to nOS (Docker provider + file provider, no K8s Gateway/CRD). PROBE (unauthenticated_endpoint_scan): the forwardAuth flow only ADDS authResponseHeaders after Authentik auth PASSES and does not forward to the backend on auth failure -> the underscore-spoof is not a pure-unauth bypass; a session must first clear the Authentik wall. RESIDUAL: (a) the forward_auth pure-gate services (Uptime Kuma, Calibre-Web, Kiwix, Puter, code-server, ntfy, Metabase, etc.) do NOT read X-authentik-* for identity -> spoof is inert there; (b) the header_oidc services that DO consume per-user headers -- Firefly III (PHP, HTTP_X_AUTHENTIK_USERNAME -> underscore collides) + KEAP (X-Authentik-uid) -- are the genuine target: an AUTHENTICATED low-priv Tier user could inject X_authentik_groups:nos-admins / X_authentik_username:<victim> to escalate or impersonate. SEC-02 network isolation does NOT cover this (edge path, not peer-container). MITIGATED to authenticated-insider escalation, not internet-anon. ACTION: bump traefik_image_version v3.6.21 -> v3.6.23 (default.config.yml + role default together; version-pin shadow) -- v3.6.23 is the latest 3.6 patch and clears CVE-2026-54763 + CVE-2026-54764 (at v3.6.22) plus the N/A ReplacePathRegex GHSA-cxjq (at v3.6.23), no config change. REM-015/025/061/075/076/077 remain resolved at the prior pins.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-16 batch-30 CVE scan (2026-07-19), Bone dependency hygiene. CVE-2026-48710 'BadHost' (GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr, disclosed 2026-05-22, fixed Starlette 1.0.1 on 2026-05-21) is an UNAUTHENTICATED host-header auth-bypass in Starlette < 1.0.1, the ASGI framework that powers FastAPI: a Host header containing '/', '?' or '#' shifts where the path begins so request.url.path no longer matches the raw ASGI scope path, letting middleware/endpoints that gate on request.url be bypassed. Bone is a FastAPI app (main.py: app=FastAPI(...)) with an UNPINNED floor fastapi>=0.115 and NO explicit starlette pin and NO committed lockfile (requirements.txt only), so a venv built before the FastAPI release that requires Starlette>=1.0.1 could transitively resolve a vulnerable Starlette. Bone is a Tier-1 manifest service routed at api.<tld> with traefik_auth_modes.bone='none' (no forward-auth wall) -> the unauth-exposed surface that makes BadHost probe-relevant. REACHABILITY = LOW / architecturally NOT exploitable: grep-confirmed bone uses NO middleware at all (no app.add_middleware, no TrustedHostMiddleware, no request.url / base_url read anywhere in *.py) -- its auth is per-route Depends(require_scope('nos:...')) which validates an Authentik-issued JWT bearer token via JWKS (auth.py, algorithms=['RS256']), keyed on the Authorization header, NOT on request.url. FastAPI routing still dispatches on the raw ASGI scope path, so require_scope fires on the actual endpoint regardless of Host-header manipulation; the only ungated route /api/health is public by design. BadHost therefore grants an attacker nothing bone doesn't already expose and does NOT bypass the scope gates -- this is supply-chain/dependency hygiene, not a live bypass. PROBE (unauthenticated_endpoint_scan): the scope-gated read endpoints (/api/services, /api/status, /api/health/aggregate) are already closed by REM-110 (resolved 2026-07-08, require_scope('nos:state:read') verified present); 127.0.0.1:8099 loopback host-bind limits direct host access. ACTION (low urgency, mirrors the wing REM-123 lockfile-discipline pattern): pin starlette>=1.0.1 (or bump the fastapi floor to a release that requires it) in files/anatomy/bone/requirements.txt AND add a committed lockfile pinning ALL bone deps (fastapi/uvicorn/httpx/PyYAML/PyJWT), the outstanding hardening item first named in the REM-110 dep-note. --- RESOLVED 2026-07-28 (bookkeeping catch-up): files/anatomy/bone/requirements.txt already carries an explicit 'starlette>=1.0.1' with a REM-128 comment, and the live bone venv reports starlette 1.3.1. The recommended ACTION was performed; only the queue entry lagged.

The SECOND half of wp2shell, untracked until now — nOS recorded only CVE-2026-63030. wp2shell is a CHAIN: CVE-2026-63030 (REST batch-route confusion) + CVE-2026-60137 (core SQL injection); chained they give unauthenticated RCE, and public exploits exist with in-the-wild exploitation reported. nOS's mu-plugin (roles/pazny.wordpress/files/cve-2026-63030-batch-block.php) unregisters /batch/v1, which breaks the chain at its entry point and is why the RCE is mitigated — but it does NOT patch the SQLi, which remains present in the pinned core 6.9.4. Residual risk is the SQLi standing alone (upstream indicates 6.8.0-6.8.5 carried the SQLi WITHOUT full chain exposure, so alone it is not RCE). BLOCKED ON THE SAME IMAGE LAG: fixed cores are 6.8.6/6.9.5/7.0.2 and the Docker official image publishes none of them; 7.0.0/7.0.1 ARE published but are in the CVE range, so they are not an escape. items.remediation_detail: Cycle-16 batch-32 SCAN (2026-07-23, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). The pinned mailpit_version v1.30.3 (roles/pazny.mailpit/defaults/main.yml; no default.config.yml shadow) is version-flagged by a THREE-advisory post-v1.30.3 cluster, and -- unlike the REM-112 cluster it succeeds -- EVERY leg is UNAUTHENTICATED and network-triggered, which makes this batch's probe focus directly applicable. (1) GHSA-w878-pj84-3j5v (MODERATE, CVSS 5.3 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N, no CVE assigned, published 2026-07-09): the SMTP/POP3 command parser buffers a whole command line with an unbounded bufio.Reader.ReadString('\n') BEFORE parsing the verb or enforcing RFC-5321's 512-octet limit -> an unauthenticated SMTP client sends one oversized newline-less command line and forces unbounded allocation. Affects <= 1.30.3, FIXED 1.30.4. (2) GHSA-75mr-qw9x-3r39 (MODERATE, CVSS 5.3, no CVE, published 2026-07-09): the thumbnail endpoint fully decodes an attacker-supplied image attachment to a raster BEFORE any dimension / decoded-pixel / memory budget check -- a 65 KB compressed PNG expands to ~64 MB decoded (>1000x amplification); triggerable by calling the API directly OR by a UI message view. Affects <= 1.30.3, FIXED 1.30.4. (3) GHSA-r553-m4fv-5v97 (MODERATE, CVSS 5.3, no CVE, published 2026-07-20): the SMTP DATA reader buffers a complete line via ReadBytes('\n') BEFORE enforcing the configured MaxMessageSize, so a single oversized unterminated line (64 MiB tested) allocates well past the cap before rejection. Affects >= v1.30.0 <= v1.30.4, FIXED v1.30.5. All three are the same availability class (C:N/I:N/A:L -- memory/CPU pressure and service degradation, not RCE or data disclosure) and all three are the continuing incomplete-fix tail of the original HIGH unauth OOM item GHSA-fpxj-m5q8-fphw / CVE-2026-45713. COVERED AT THE PIN (re-verified, no action): CVE-2026-55187 (GHSA-w4mc-hhc6-xp28, IPv6 SSRF-guard bypass, fix 1.30.2), CVE-2026-48824 (GHSA-28pq-6qxg-wg5r, unbounded-JSON DoS on /api/v1/messages + /api/v1/tags + /api/v1/message/{id}/release, MED 5.3, fix 1.30.1), CVE-2026-45713 (fix 1.29.8), CVE-2026-27808 (GHSA-mpf7-p9x7-96r3, Link Check SSRF, fix 1.29.2), CVE-2026-22689 (CSWSH, fix 1.28.2), CVE-2026-23829 (SMTP header injection, fix 1.28.3) -- i.e. REM-081..085 + REM-112 all stay resolved at v1.30.3. PROBE (unauthenticated_endpoint_scan) / MITIGATION: mailpit is the ONLY component in this batch that is install_mailpit=true BY DEFAULT, so version hygiene genuinely matters here. But the compose template maps ONLY 127.0.0.1:8025 (UI/REST) and 127.0.0.1:1025 (SMTP) -- UNCONDITIONALLY, with no services_lan_access escape hatch (unlike ntfy/onlyoffice/erpnext) -- and traefik_auth_modes.mailpit='proxy' puts authentik@file forward-auth in front of the UI + REST + thumbnail endpoints at mail.<tld>. So the thumbnail-decode leg is NOT anonymously edge-reachable. RESIDUAL (the honest part): the SMTP listener has no auth by design and is reachable from (a) any host-local process and (b) every container on the shared docker network that can resolve mailpit:1025 -- which is exactly what the sink exists for. So the two SMTP legs degrade to a container-local / host-local DoS, not an internet-anon one. NOT internet-exploitable; NOT a confidentiality or integrity issue. ACTION: bump mailpit_version v1.30.3 -> v1.30.5 (latest, released 2026-07-20) in roles/pazny.mailpit/defaults/main.yml. Pure image-tag bump, no config change. --- RESOLVED 2026-07-28 (bookkeeping catch-up): mailpit_version is ALREADY 'v1.30.5' (roles/pazny.mailpit/defaults/main.yml:21, no default.config.yml shadow) and iiab-mailpit-1 is RUNNING axllent/mailpit:v1.30.5 — the exact recommended target, closing all three post-v1.30.3 advisories.

Cycle-16 batch-32 SCAN (2026-07-23, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). SUCCESSOR to REM-124 (resolved 2026-07-16 -- the pin advanced v2.22.0 -> v2.23.0, live-verified iiab-ntfy-1 on binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.23.0, which closed the SVG-attachment-preview stored XSS GHSA-j8hr-p342-xrmh). The pin is now 3 minors + 3 patches behind latest v2.26.3 (2026-07-20), and each intervening minor carries an UNADVISED security fix -- ntfy's GitHub security-advisories page is EMPTY (0 published advisories) and OSV.dev/GHSA carry no ntfy entries, so these are release-note-level only, with NO CVE and NO vendor CVSS. Rated MEDIUM here on the token-predictability leg; do NOT cite a CVE for it. (1) v2.24.0 -- 'Fix case-insensitive ACL topic matching on SQLite': an access-control CORRECTNESS bug where topic ACL rules did not match as intended under SQLite, i.e. authorization could resolve differently than the administrator wrote it. (2) v2.25.0 -- 'Generate access tokens, IDs, and magic-link tokens with a cryptographically secure RNG (crypto/rand) instead of a clock-seeded PRNG': this is the significant one. A clock-seeded math/rand stream makes issued access tokens and magic-link tokens PREDICTABLE to an attacker who can constrain the seed (issuance time) -- a credential-guessing / auth-bypass class, and the only leg in this item with any unauthenticated-endpoint relevance (guessing a valid bearer token needs no prior session). (3) v2.26.0 -- 'Prevent a CPU denial of service via message templates (Template: yes)': template execution is now hard-capped with an execution timeout; before the cap, a publisher-supplied template could burn CPU unbounded. v2.26.3 (latest) carries no further security content. PROBE (unauthenticated_endpoint_scan) / MITIGATION: no anonymous reach. install_ntfy=false (off by default); traefik_auth_modes.ntfy='proxy' so authentik@file forward-auth gates the web UI, admin surface AND the publish/API paths at ntfy.<tld>; the server config keeps auth-default-access=deny-all + enable-signup=false; the container host-maps only 127.0.0.1:2586 (LAN bind only when services_lan_access=true). The token-predictability leg is therefore reachable only by someone who already cleared the Authentik wall, and the template-DoS leg needs publish rights -> insider-scoped, not internet-anon. CVE-2026-39087 (SSRF via unanchored web-push URL regex, NVD 6.4 -- the widely-syndicated 'parseActions RCE' framing remains an AI-generated mislabel that contradicts NVD) stays RESOLVED via REM-087 at v2.22.0, re-verified. ACTION (defense-in-depth): bump ntfy_version v2.23.0 -> v2.26.3 in roles/pazny.ntfy/defaults/main.yml. Note the v2.25.0 RNG change does NOT retroactively rotate already-issued tokens -- if ntfy is ever enabled with tokens minted on <= v2.24.x, re-issue them after the bump.

Cycle-16 batch-33 SCAN (2026-07-24, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). SUCCESSOR to REM-098 (resolved; its target 1.31.2+ is now itself version-flagged). The nginx.org advisory page carries a NEW post-1.31.2 wave, all three fixed in 1.31.3+ / 1.30.4+. HEADLINE CVE-2026-42533 (severity MAJOR per nginx.org): buffer overflow when using `map` with a regex; affects 0.9.6-1.31.2 -- i.e. EVERY nginx release prior to 1.31.3, including whatever the host package currently resolves to. APPLICABILITY IS DIRECT, not latent: templates/nginx/nginx.conf:103 defines `map $uri $conn_limit_key { ~*\.(js|css|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|svg|ico|woff2?|ttf|eot|map|webp)$ ""; default $binary_remote_addr; }` -- a map keyed on the REQUEST URI with a case-insensitive regex arm, which is precisely the vulnerable construct. Because the map key is $uri, the regex is evaluated against an ATTACKER-CONTROLLED, UNAUTHENTICATED request path on EVERY request, before any auth/proxy decision -- this is the probe-focus leg. A second regex-free map exists in sites-available/code-server.conf:10 (`map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade`, literal arms only, not vulnerable). SUCCESSOR to REM-103, NOT a re-open: REM-103 was correctly RESOLVED on 2026-07-13 when the pin moved off the EOL floating '8.0' tag (final 8.0.6) onto 8.6.3 (default.config.yml:1140 + roles/pazny.redis/defaults/main.yml:14, in sync), clearing the May-2026 DarkReplica cluster (CVE-2026-23479 / 25243 / 25588 / 25589 / 23631) that had NO 8.0.x backport. Since then upstream published 8.6.4 (2026-06-04) and 8.6.5 (2026-07-23). Redis 8.6.5 carries the release-notes tag 'Upgrade Urgency: SECURITY' -- Redis's highest -- and fixes TWO RCE-class memory-corruption bugs absent from the pinned 8.6.3, shipped as a coordinated multi-branch wave (8.8.1 / 8.6.5 / 8.4.5 / 8.2.8 / 7.4.10 / 7.2.15 / 6.2.23, all published within ~90 minutes on 2026-07-23). (1) CORE, APPLIES: a malicious stream RESTORE payload can make two consumers point at the SAME pending-entry NACK record, so removing both consumers frees the same object twice -- a use-after-free / double-free potentially enabling remote code execution. This is in core Streams, present in the stock redis image. (2) P1046, N/A BY CONFIG: crafted RESTORE payloads in the RedisBloom and TDigest modules trigger out-of-bounds writes, potentially leading to RCE -- the stock redis:8.6.x image loads NO modules (compose.yml.j2 command is redis-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru --requirepass ..., no --loadmodule), exactly the same N/A-by-config disposition that retired CVE-2026-25588/25589 in REM-103. NO CVE IDs assigned yet and Redis's own 8.6.5 notes carry no CVSS -- confidence HIGH on existence (verbatim upstream release notes, security urgency tag, coordinated 7-branch wave), MEDIUM on precise severity scoring. Filed HIGH for consistency with REM-103, whose CVE-2026-23479/25243 are the same authenticated-RESTORE/UAF-to-RCE class scored 7.7 by Redis. MITIGATED, exactly as REM-103 was: RESTORE is a normal command requiring an AUTHENTICATED connection, and the deployment binds 127.0.0.1:{{ redis_port|6379 }} loopback only (compose.yml.j2 ports) with --requirepass set unconditionally (REM-003/REM-012) plus infra_net / shared_net / gated_b2b_net internal reachability; there is no HTTP surface and no LAN bind unless services_lan_access=true. So the practical attacker is an already-authenticated client or a compromised in-stack service (authentik, outline, superset, erpnext, firefly), not an anonymous remote. PROBE (unauthenticated_endpoint_scan): pre-auth network surface remains NIL -- no HTTP/edge endpoint, no Traefik router (no domain_var in state/manifest.yml), loopback-only host bind, password required before any command including RESTORE. In-branch patch bump, no RDB/AOF format change, no migration; note 8.6.4 additionally fixed an AArch64 startup failure, directly relevant on Apple Silicon. Cycle-16 batch-36 SCAN (2026-07-28, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). NOT a CVE -- currency/hygiene item, filed so a Tier-1 secrets vault's pin does not silently rot (same class as REM-135 spacetimedb, but on a DEFAULT-ON component). The CVE leg is CLEAN and re-confirmed for the fourth consecutive batch: the Infisical/infisical GitHub Security Advisories endpoint returns an EMPTY list (zero advisories ever published), and prior batches cleared OSV.dev, the GitHub Advisory DB and NVD (keywordSearch=infisical, totalResults 0). The 2026 search near-hits remain OTHER vendors (Tenda router CVE-2026-4041, Gardyn IoT CVE-2026-54477) and, this batch, a large volume of n8n RCE coverage (CVE-2026-21858 / 21877) that is a different product entirely. WHAT CHANGED: the pinned infisical_version v0.160.4 (default.config.yml:2610 + roles/pazny.infisical/defaults/main.yml:10, in sync, shadow already cleared) now trails upstream by two minor lines -- latest is v0.162.14 (2026-07-27), with releases landing near-daily (v0.162.5 through v0.162.14 all shipped 2026-07-13..27). No release in that span is flagged as a security fix and no GHSA backs any of them, so severity is LOW and confidence on 'no known vulnerability' is HIGH. STANDING CAVEAT, unchanged and the reason this is tracked at all: Infisical uses PRIVATE disclosure (security@infisical.com + Cure53 engagements) and publishes no advisories, so a fixed-but-unadvised issue can ship silently inside an ordinary release -- for this vendor, version currency IS the security control, because there will never be a CVE to trigger a bump. That asymmetry is what lifts this above pure hygiene: unlike spacetimedb (install=false), install_infisical=true by DEFAULT and Infisical is the Tier-1 central secrets vault holding infra credentials, so an unadvised fix left unapplied has real blast radius. PROBE (unauthenticated_endpoint_scan): NO unauth exposure, re-verified. SUCCESSOR to REM-118 (resolved), not a re-open: the pin correctly advanced php8.3-1.17.159 -> 2.1.3-php8.3 and closed the CVE-2026-53595 CRITICAL 9.4 unauth account-takeover leg. But nfrastack 2.1.3-php8.3 (image published 2026-06-27) bundles FreeScout app 1.8.226, and upstream has since shipped FIVE app releases, THREE of which are explicitly security releases: 1.8.227 (2026-07-04, GHSA-v8vc-cmf9-gg2c + dependency library patches), 1.8.230 (2026-07-18, 'Improved remote URL sanitizing' GHSA-6w8v-qp43-vg2h + 'Send CSP header in /ajax-html/ URLs' GHSA-2g42-f97q-973x), 1.8.231 (2026-07-25, 'Check customer visibility in load_customer_info ajax action' GHSA-cr68-27qv-p5m4 + 'Restricted access to Assigned Conversations option in user profiles' GHSA-m4hc-rc98-38jc + 'Change customer when received a reply to a conversation from completely new email address' GHSA-j49f-9g94-3wh4 + 'Tighten throttling in Forgot Password requests' GHSA-jvmv-2qcp-7855). KEY EVIDENCE / WHY THIS IS FILED AT MEDIUM WITH MEDIUM CONFIDENCE ON SEVERITY: six of those seven GHSA IDs are UNPUBLISHED in the GitHub global advisory database -- `gh api advisories/<id>` returns 404 for GHSA-v8vc-cmf9-gg2c, GHSA-6w8v-qp43-vg2h, GHSA-2g42-f97q-973x, GHSA-cr68-27qv-p5m4, GHSA-m4hc-rc98-38jc and GHSA-j49f-9g94-3wh4, and none appears in the repo's 93 published advisories. So these are REAL security fixes shipped in tagged releases with NO public CVSS, NO CVE and NO affected-range metadata. A version-keyed scanner sees nothing; only the release-note prose reveals them. Confidence HIGH on the version-lag fact (release notes are authoritative), MEDIUM on severity (no published vector to score). The only one that IS published, GHSA-jvmv-2qcp-7855 / CVE-2026-45294 (MODERATE 5.3, unauth agent-email enumeration via password-reset response differentiation), is patched at 1.8.219 and therefore ALREADY covered by the pin -- 1.8.231 merely tightens the throttling further. RE-VERIFIED COVERED (no action): the entire 2026-07-15 published advisory batch is patched at <=1.8.226 and so is already closed by the pin -- GHSA-gh3r-jh6q-wrvj / CVE-2026-62856 (HIGH 7.7, cross-user notification disclosure via LIKE-wildcard injection in the polycast channel query; notable because the polycast routes lack the auth middleware, so any visitor holding a session+CSRF token reaches it), GHSA-jpq8-j69f-mj98 / CVE-2026-62854 (HIGH 7.6, stored XSS in mailbox signature via same-origin JS upload), GHSA-w668-wq26-6c94 / CVE-2026-62852 (MED 6.5), GHSA-wqq7-4q7m-273v / CVE-2026-62851 (MED 4.3), GHSA-62855 path traversal + GHSA-w2p9 tools.php (both <=1.8.225). PROBE (unauthenticated_endpoint_scan): traefik_auth_modes.freescout='oidc' -> native OIDC, 200 at edge, FreeScout owns its login page and is NOT forward-auth gated; install_freescout=true (default-on, b2b stack); 127.0.0.1:8090 loopback host-bind (services_lan_access=false) blocks the direct port but NOT the Traefik route. Probe-relevant residual among the unpublished set: GHSA-j49f-9g94-3wh4 rebinds a conversation's customer when a reply arrives from a completely new email address -- inbound email is an UNAUTHENTICATED input channel and this is the same class as the previously-patched CVE-2026-53591 thread-injection leg, so it is the most likely pre-auth item in the batch (unconfirmed: advisory unpublished). Recommend the 2.1.5-php8.3 drop-in now and a separately-verified 2.2.1 move once php8.5 compatibility is exercised (or wait for a 2.2.x php8.3 tag). REM-029/069/070/071/118 all remain resolved.

NOT a CVE -- supply-chain reproducibility + currency item that PROMOTES the standing 'repin off the floating feature-SHA to a tagged release' recommendation (carried as prose in scan-state since 2026-07-02) into a tracked queue entry, because the blocker that justified the SHA has now been disproven. The in-repo comments at default.config.yml:2206 ('ghcr.io/paperclipai/paperclip (no semver tags published)') and roles/pazny.paperclip/defaults/main.yml:11 ('upstream publishes only latest (no fixed/semver tags)') are FACTUALLY STALE: `gh api repos/paperclipai/paperclip/releases` returns dated release tags -- v2026.722.0 (2026-07-22), v2026.720.0, v2026.707.0, v2026.626.0, v2026.618.0, v2026.609.0 -- i.e. the same v2026.MMDD.0 scheme as the v2026.416.0 fix release the pin is already described against. The pinned sha-b9a80dc is a 2026-04-17 commit, so the pin now trails upstream by roughly three months and six releases while remaining a mutable, non-reproducible feature-SHA reference. CVE LEG: no NEW published-and-applicable advisory -- every item on the paperclipai/paperclip advisories page with a patched version is fixed at v2026.416.0 and therefore already covered by the pinned descendant commit (CVE-2026-41679 CRIT unauth import-authz RCE, CVE-2026-41208 HIGH provisionCommand injection, GHSA-vr7g-88fq-vhq3 CRIT cleanupCommand OS-command-injection, GHSA-3xx2-mqjm-hg9x + GHSA-47wq-cj9q-wpmp CRIT cross-tenant agent-key IDOR/minting, GHSA-xfqj-r5qw-8g4j HIGH unauth access to multiple API endpoints in authenticated mode, GHSA-w8hx-hqjv-vjcq, GHSA-p7mm-r948-4q3q, GHSA-fpw4-p57j-hqmq, GHSA-3pw3-v88x-xj24). THE ONE NEW ADVISORY THIS BATCH IS **N/A BY VERIFIED CONFIGURATION** -- see the vuln-report entry: GHSA-x8hx-rhr2-9rf7 (CRITICAL, CVSS 9.6 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H, CWE-862 + CWE-1188, published 2026-07-22, range '<0.3.1', patched_versions field EMPTY = unpatched at publication) -- drive-by unauthenticated RCE against LOCAL Paperclip instances via DNS rebinding, and it explicitly defeats a 127.0.0.1 bind. nOS is NOT affected, verified by reading the pinned commit's own source rather than inferring from the advisory prose: (1) roles/pazny.paperclip/templates/compose.yml.j2:32 sets PAPERCLIP_DEPLOYMENT_MODE='authenticated', and server/src/middleware/auth.ts@b9a80dc line 25 scopes the auto-admin actor ({isInstanceAdmin:true, source:'local_implicit'}) to deploymentMode==='local_trusted' ONLY -- in authenticated mode a rebound request arrives as actor {type:'none'}; (2) server/src/config.ts@b9a80dc line 179 defaults deploymentExposure to 'private' when PAPERCLIP_DEPLOYMENT_EXPOSURE is unset (nOS does not set it), and server/src/app.ts@b9a80dc lines 96-97 enable the private-hostname guard when exposure==='private' && (local_trusted||authenticated) -- so the Host-header guard IS ACTIVE on the pinned build; (3) the guard (server/src/middleware/private-hostname-guard.ts@b9a80dc) reads x-forwarded-host then host, and 403s any hostname outside {localhost,127.0.0.1,::1} + the registered allowlist, which roles/pazny.paperclip/tasks/post.yml:65-84 populates NARROWLY via `pnpm paperclipai allowed-hostname {{ paperclip_domain }}` plus service_extra_hosts -- an attacker's rebinding domain is not on it. Two independent controls, both source-verified at the pinned SHA. NO ACTION IS REQUIRED FOR THE CRITICAL; this item is the currency leg only. FORWARD RISK THIS BOUNDS: the guard is the sole structural defense against the rebinding class, and it is silently disabled by setting PAPERCLIP_DEPLOYMENT_EXPOSURE to a non-'private' value -- treat that env var as security-relevant and never introduce it as a route-debugging workaround; the correct fix for a blocked hostname is to register it via the post.yml allowlist task. ACTION: repin paperclip_version 'sha-b9a80dc' -> 'v2026.722.0' in default.config.yml:2206 AND roles/pazny.paperclip/defaults/main.yml:11, and correct the stale 'no semver tags published' comments in both files. auto_fixable=false: this is a three-month code advance on an agent-orchestration service with a Postgres schema, so it needs a supervised converge (DB migration + the post.yml CEO-bootstrap and allowed-hostname re-registration path) rather than a mechanical tag swap. items.remediation_detail: Cycle-17 batch-38 SCAN (2026-07-30, version_header_leakage). LIVE-CONFIRMED, NOT theoretical -- this is the probe's finding of record and it OVERTURNS the standing 'dashboard + api.insecure bound 127.0.0.1:8080 loopback' disposition that has been carried in scan-state for traefik since batch-21. The loopback bind is real but IRRELEVANT: state/manifest.yml:145-153 gives the traefik entry BOTH domain_var (traefik_domain) and port_var (traefik_dashboard_port), so roles/pazny.traefik/templates/dynamic/services.yml.j2 auto-derives a file-provider router for it -- and roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml sets traefik_auth_modes.traefik='none' with the now-FALSE inline comment "own dashboard (LAN-only via 127.0.0.1 bind)". Router as rendered live (GET /api/rawdata): {"traefik@file": entryPoints:[websecure], rule: Host(`traefik.<tld>`), middlewares: [security-headers@file, compress@file], service -> http://192.168.65.254:8082}. There is NO authentik@file in that middleware chain, and the backend URL is the Docker host-gateway address -- i.e. Traefik itself proxies AROUND the 127.0.0.1 bind it was supposed to be protected by. Combined with api.insecure:true + api.dashboard:true in roles/pazny.traefik/templates/traefik.yml.j2, the ENTIRE Traefik API is anonymous over HTTPS:443. LIVE EVIDENCE (unauthenticated GET, Host header only, no cookie/token): /api/version -> 200 {"Version":"3.6.23","Codename":"ramequin"}; /dashboard/ -> 200; /api/overview -> 200 (54 routers / 52 services / 13 middlewares); /api/rawdata -> 200, 35670 bytes = the complete edge topology (every router rule, every internal backend URL and port, every middleware); /api/http/middlewares -> 200, 4971 bytes. THE CRITICAL LEG IS SECRET DISCLOSURE, not version disclosure. /api/http/middlewares serves the rendered `headers.customRequestHeaders` maps VERBATIM, which means the two SEC-6 edge-trust tokens are readable by any anonymous client: (1) face-edge@file -> X-Face-Edge-Token: '<prefix>_pw_face_edge'; (2) wing-edge@file -> X-Wing-Edge-Token: '<64-hex>'. Both tokens exist SOLELY on the premise, documented in middlewares.yml.j2 itself, that 'only Traefik (which holds the token) can present it' and that customRequestHeaders REPLACES any client-sent value so 'a peer on gated_net cannot pre-poison it'. That premise is now false at the FRONT of the proxy rather than behind it. Consequences: X-Face-Edge-Token is the exact condition under which the nOS face BFF (files/anatomy/face, src/hooks.server.ts) TRUSTS attacker-supplied X-Authentik-* identity headers -> forge the pair and impersonate any user including nos-admins; X-Wing-Edge-Token defeats Wing's BasePresenter::startup() edge gate, the second half of the SEC-6 defense-in-depth pair whose first half (the 127.0.0.1 Caddyfile bind) is likewise bypassable via a Traefik route. WORST LEG -- PREFIX DISCLOSURE: default.credentials.yml:421 defines face_edge_token as the literal template '{{ global_password_prefix }}_pw_face_edge', so the leaked header value discloses global_password_prefix IN CLEARTEXT (live host: the prefix was recovered verbatim from the anonymous response). That single string is the seed for EVERY unset credential in default.credentials.yml -- the whole '{global_password_prefix}_pw_{service}' family -- so an anonymous reader can DERIVE, without further interaction, any service password the operator did not explicitly override: woodpecker_agent_secret, the DB passwords, mysqld_exporter_password, akadmin_password, the authentik_oidc_*_client_secret seed twins, etc. This converts an information-disclosure bug into a full credential-derivation compromise of the tenant. REACHABILITY (stated honestly, do not overclaim): CONFIRMED anonymous over HTTPS from the LAN/Tailscale surface -- Traefik binds 0.0.0.0:443 and the only precondition is the ability to reach the host on 443 and set the Host header. The hostname IS publicly resolvable (dig @1.1.1.1 traefik.<tld> -> Cloudflare 188.114.96.9/97.9), but INTERNET reachability could NOT be verified from inside the LAN: split-horizon DNS (dnsmasq) resolves the name to the host's own LAN address, so the 'public' curl in this batch provably transited the LAN (remote_ip was the 192.168.x host), NOT the Cloudflare edge. Whether CF proxies through to this origin is UNVERIFIED and must be checked from an off-net vantage point before rating internet exposure. ACTION (any one closes the anonymous leg; do at least the first): (1) set traefik_auth_modes.traefik: 'proxy' in roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml so authentik@file gates the router -- note this is a Tier-1 admin surface and 'none' was never a defensible mode for it; or add 'traefik' to traefik_skip_ids so no edge router is derived at all. (2) Set api.insecure:false in traefik.yml.j2 (the dashboard then requires an explicit secured router) -- defense in depth even after (1). (3) INDEPENDENT of the routing fix, treat the exposed values as BURNED: rotate global_password_prefix, wing_edge_token and face_edge_token, and stop deriving edge tokens from the prefix -- default.credentials.yml:420-421 already carry an 'openssl rand -hex 32' comment that wing_edge_token honours (it rendered as 64-hex) and face_edge_token does NOT (it rendered as the prefix template). Making face_edge_token an independently-generated secret removes the prefix-disclosure leg even if a header is leaked again. (4) Consider a repo gate asserting that no manifest entry with a domain_var maps to traefik_auth_modes 'none' unless explicitly allowlisted -- the root cause is that 'none' silently means 'anonymous at the edge', the same general lesson batch-34 recorded for native_oidc services.

SECRET LEG: face_edge_token joined the main.yml regeneration group AND templates/secrets.yml.j2 persistence (it was in neither — its sibling wing_edge_token was in both), so it is a 256-bit random persisted secret instead of {prefix}_pw_face_edge; the global password prefix is no longer on the edge surface. items.remediation_detail: Cycle-17 batch-38 SCAN (2026-07-30, version_header_leakage). NEW advisory published 2026-07-27T09:02:31Z -- i.e. AFTER the last traefik look (batch-28, 2026-07-15) and after the v3.6.23 pin that REM-127 landed. GHSA-3ccp-42pg-hgv6, 'Cross-user response poisoning via proxied CONNECT on Traefik's shared backend keep-alive pool'. NO CVE ID assigned yet. CVSS 4.0 = 7.0 HIGH, vector CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N, CWE-444 (HTTP request/response smuggling). Affected: v2.x <= 2.11.52 (fix 2.11.53), v3.6 <= 3.6.23 (fix 3.6.24), v3.7 <= 3.7.8 (fix 3.7.9); all three fix releases shipped 2026-07-24. The pinned traefik_image_version v3.6.23 (default.config.yml:1869 + roles/pazny.traefik/defaults/main.yml:16, in sync) is the TOP of the v3.6 affected range. MECHANISM: Traefik's default httputil.ReverseProxy forwards a client CONNECT request -- with a live body stream -- to an HTTP/1.1 upstream instead of rejecting it. If that upstream answers a keep-alive NON-2xx without draining the request body, the now-desynchronised backend socket is returned to Traefik's SHARED connection pool; the next client to draw that socket receives responses queued from the attacker's smuggled requests. Impact is unauthenticated cross-user response poisoning -- one user is served another user's response, potentially authenticated/private content -- and with a bounded pool a single desync can poison a whole response queue, hitting multiple victims. APPLICABILITY TO nOS = YES, both preconditions are met and were verified live this batch, not assumed. (1) FRONTEND must be HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 (HTTP/1.1 frontends are unaffected): every edge probe in this batch negotiated h2 over the websecure entrypoint -- responses came back as literal 'HTTP/2 200' -- because traefik.yml.j2 terminates TLS on websecure and Go's server offers h2 via ALPN by default. (2) BACKEND must answer a keep-alive non-2xx without draining; the advisory explicitly names Go net/http and gunicorn/Flask upstreams as remaining exploitable, and nOS's Tier-1 upstream fleet is full of both -- woodpecker-server is Go net/http, calibre-web is Flask/Werkzeug (live-confirmed this batch: '302 FOUND' with Werkzeug-style uppercase reason phrase), plus the Python/uvicorn and Node/Express services behind the same edge. The advisory notes the default sanitizePath option is only an INCOMPLETE mitigation. Not provider-specific (not a Kubernetes-only item, unlike most of the recent traefik advisory wave). ACTION: bump v3.6.23 -> v3.6.24 in default.config.yml:1869 AND roles/pazny.traefik/defaults/main.yml:16 together (version-pin-shadow discipline). Patch-level move within the 3.6 line, no config change. Documented risk-reducers if the bump must be deferred: maxIdleConnsPerHost:-1 to disable backend pooling, or the experimental FastProxy implementation. ALSO SURFACED THIS BATCH, N/A: GHSA-8rxv-jg7p-wvg3 (HIGH, 2026-07-16, Kubernetes Ingress NGINX RewriteTarget path-traversal route-level auth bypass) -- Kubernetes Ingress-NGINX provider ONLY, and nOS runs the Docker + file providers with no K8s provider configured. REM-127 stays RESOLVED (its v3.6.21 -> v3.6.23 bump landed and is live: the running container is traefik:v3.6.23 and /api/version self-reports 3.6.23).

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-17 batch-38 SCAN (2026-07-30, version_header_leakage). CVE LEG IS CLEAN -- an OSV version-aware query for go.woodpecker-ci.org/woodpecker/v3@3.14.1 returns exactly 2 entries and they are the same finding twice (GHSA-qf34-295c-26v8 = GO-2026-5992 = CVE-2026-61549, HIGH, unrestricted serviceAccountName pipeline-pod privilege escalation, affected 1.0.0-3.15.0, fix 3.16.0), which is KUBERNETES-BACKEND-ONLY and therefore N/A: roles/pazny.woodpecker/templates/compose.yml.j2 hard-sets WOODPECKER_BACKEND=docker. Nothing has been published on the repo since that advisory (2026-07-01); the two other titles that surface in a naive web search, GHSA-4gcf-5m39-98mc and GHSA-xw35-rrcp-g7xm, were fetched and are CVE-2023-40034 (fix 1.0.2) and CVE-2024-41121 (fix 2.7.0) -- both years old and both far below the pin. REM-105 and REM-002 stay resolved. PROBE FINDING (version_header_leakage), LIVE-CONFIRMED: Woodpecker's /version endpoint is anonymously readable THROUGH THE TRAEFIK EDGE, not merely on loopback. Unauthenticated GET https://ci.<tld>/version -> HTTP/2 200 {"source":"https://github.com/woodpecker-ci/woodpecker","version":"3.14.1"} and GET / -> 200 serving the SPA shell. No version-bearing RESPONSE HEADER is emitted (no Server, no X-Powered-By -- Go net/http sends none), so the leak is a body-level version oracle rather than a header one. IMPORTANT DISPOSITION CORRECTION: every prior scan-state note for woodpecker (batch-16 and batch-28) recorded the mitigation as 'forward_auth (Authentik gates the route) + Gitea OAuth2 app-auth'. THAT IS WRONG and CLAUDE.md repeats it ('Woodpecker (route gate on top of Gitea-OAuth app-auth)' in the forward_auth bucket). roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml sets traefik_auth_modes.woodpecker='oidc', with an explicit inline rationale -- a forward-auth gate would be the documented double-login anti-pattern AND would 302 the playbook's own Woodpecker API post-wiring -- so there is NO authentik@file middleware on this router and the edge answers anonymously. The live probe confirms it. The 127.0.0.1:8060/:9060 host binds constrain only the direct container ports, never the Traefik path (the same lesson batch-34 recorded for vaultwarden and this batch re-learned, far more expensively, for traefik itself in REM-144). SEVERITY IS LOW and the 'oidc' mode remains the right call: the exposure is precise-version disclosure plus an SPA shell, every API call still 401s, and login still redirects to Gitea OAuth -- no data exposure. It is filed because an exact-version oracle at an internet-facing edge lets an attacker pre-stage the next Woodpecker advisory against a known-vulnerable build with zero noise, and because the RECORDED mitigation was materially false and would have mis-scoped any future finding on this component. install_woodpecker=false by default (though it IS running on the live host). ACTION: (a) correct the woodpecker disposition here and in the CLAUDE.md SSO trichotomy -- it belongs in the native_oidc bucket, not forward_auth; (b) OPTIONAL currency bump v3.14.1 -> v3.16.0 in default.config.yml:1552 + roles/pazny.woodpecker/defaults/main.yml:14, which also moves the pin out of the GHSA-qf34 affected range so version-keyed scanners stop flagging it even though the bug is N/A here; (c) no action available on /version itself -- it is unauthenticated by upstream design and gating it would break the app-auth model.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-17 batch-38 SCAN (2026-07-30, version_header_leakage). CVE LEG IS CLEAN at the pinned jellyfin_version 10.11.10 (default.config.yml:1602 + roles/pazny.jellyfin/defaults/main.yml:10, in sync). Every advisory on the repo was re-pulled with fix versions this batch and all are at or below the pin: CVE-2026-48793 (GHSA-wwwm-px48-fpvq, HIGH 8.8, unauth FFmpeg arg-injection in the subtitle path) range <10.11.10 patched 10.11.10; CVE-2026-49247 (MED, authed /ClientLog/Document path traversal) patched 10.11.10; CVE-2026-49246 (LOW, MKV attachment filename traversal to RCE) patched 10.11.10; CVE-2026-49220 (MED 5.7, user-management XSS) patched 10.11.9; the April cluster CVE-2026-35031/35032/35033/35034 patched 10.11.7. NOTHING has been published since 2026-06-10. Latest 10.11.x is 10.11.11 (2026-06-06, the regression-fix release for 10.11.7 breakage, no security content); the v12.0 line is at rc3 (2026-07-22) and is PRE-RELEASE -- do not move to it. REM-033/072/119 all stay resolved. PROBE FINDING (version_header_leakage), LIVE-CONFIRMED: Jellyfin is the batch's clearest textbook case, leaking on BOTH channels. (1) RESPONSE HEADER: every response carries 'Server: Kestrel', disclosing the ASP.NET Core stack. (2) BODY: unauthenticated GET https://media.<tld>/System/Info/Public -> HTTP/2 200 returning {"LocalAddress","ServerName","Version":"10.11.10","ProductName","OperatingSystem","Id","StartupWizardCompleted"} -- an exact version oracle plus the container hostname as ServerName plus a stable 32-hex server Id usable as a cross-session tracking identifier. Anonymous, no cookie, no token, straight through the Traefik edge. WHY IT IS ANONYMOUS AT THE EDGE: traefik_auth_modes.jellyfin='oidc' (native SSO via the 9p4 SSO-Auth plugin), so no authentik@file middleware is attached and the router forwards anonymous traffic; /System/Info/Public is unauthenticated by upstream design (clients need it for discovery). AMPLIFIER, unchanged from batch-16/28 and re-confirmed live: jellyfin_lan_access defaults TRUE in BOTH default.config.yml:1603 and the role default, so the container publishes 0.0.0.0:8096 (docker ps live: '0.0.0.0:8096->8096/tcp, [::]:8096->8096/tcp'), not a loopback bind -- this is the ONE service in this batch whose raw port is LAN-reachable independently of Traefik, and the SSO-Auth plugin does not gate that raw port. So the disclosure is reachable by two independent paths. SEVERITY LOW: pure information disclosure, no authentication or integrity impact, and the leg that made this combination genuinely dangerous (CVE-2026-48793, unauth FFmpeg arg-injection on a LAN-reachable port) is PATCHED at the current pin. It is filed rather than dropped because the exact-version oracle is what makes the NEXT unauth Jellyfin advisory instantly targetable on this host, and because install_jellyfin=false is the documented mitigation yet the service is in fact RUNNING on the live host (jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.10) -- the 'default-off' framing should stop being counted as a control for this tenant. ACTION (all optional, none urgent): (a) set jellyfin_lan_access=false unless TV/mobile clients genuinely need the raw port, which removes the second path; (b) if the raw port must stay, accept that /System/Info/Public is un-gateable and treat the version as public -- i.e. keep the pin current aggressively, since disclosure plus lag is the actual risk; (c) 'Server: Kestrel' cannot be removed upstream but a Traefik customResponseHeaders entry setting Server to empty on this router would strip it at the edge -- cosmetic, and it does nothing for the raw-port path.
